selection.angle: Southwest cuts its full-year adjusted earnings outlook despite stronger fares, record quarterly revenue and a quarterly earnings beat. Explain how current operating gains and pressure on the next quarter can coexist.
selection.evidence_plan: Use only retained goal35-southwest Reuters facts, published 2026-10-21T20:23:00Z, known 2026-10-21T22:27:23.031Z. Attribute issuer guidance through Reuters: 2026 adjusted EPS expected $2.60-$2.85 versus prior $3.25-$4.25; this proves the reported forecasting act, not future achieved earnings. Retain supplied statement that new midpoint is below $2.85 LSEG analyst average without manual midpoint calculation. Bind nearly 27% Q3 average passenger fare increase, Q3 record $8.4bn revenue, higher adjusted operating margin despite fuel costs, fuel bill +$821m year on year, and Q3 adjusted EPS 66 cents versus 58-cent expectation and 11 cents year ago. Final-quarter jet-fuel increase is company expectation only. Do not infer fare increase equals yield, demand or passenger-volume growth; do not calculate fuel sensitivity or attribute entire guidance reduction to fuel. Keep Q3 results and full-year/future expectations separate. Accepted historical 2025 hedge/AOCI case remains dated history; this current report neither independently updates hedge status nor contradicts or invalidates that case. Missing: exact margin, traffic/capacity/mix, fuel-volume/unit-cost split and earnings bridge. Code owns arithmetic. No new retrieval, requests, quotes or media.
selection.primary_reader_question: Why can Southwest beat quarterly earnings expectations and raise fares yet cut its full-year profit outlook?
research_queries: Southwest October 21 2026 profit forecast fares fuel costs adjusted earnings
selection.selection_rationale: The fresh 2026 guidance change creates an actionable reading question about revenue strength versus earnings exposure, not a recycled hedge-accounting explainer. Concrete reported quarterly gains make a serious countercase to a simple deterioration narrative. Only Southwest selected; prior oil, IBM, Tesla and Meta remain handled.

comparison: Current FX remains a separate operation. Historical Southwest hedge closure and AOCI research addresses different dates and accounting clocks; no contradiction from current earnings report is established. Other retained SEC, custody, Fed/FX and public Main/EIA research supplies neither fresh Southwest confirmation nor a reason to recycle prior explainers. Seven published identities were deterministically filtered; no full published corpus is supplied, so no exhaustive independent history audit is claimed.
mechanism: Higher fares and quarterly revenue can coexist with rising input costs and weaker prospective earnings. A quarterly beat compares actual Q3 EPS with expectations; a full-year outlook incorporates later expectations and is not the same comparison.
countercase: Reported higher adjusted operating margin and stronger quarterly adjusted EPS show operating improvements despite higher fuel costs. They prevent treating the guidance cut as proof that the turnaround failed. Conversely, a quarterly beat does not establish protection against prospective fuel pressure.
watch_conditions: A comparable earnings bridge separating fare/mix, traffic, nonfuel expenses and fuel price/volume would test which forces explain the revised outlook.
Later realized fuel prices and quarterly outcomes could test company expectations; current guidance is not future truth. No new requests are authorized by these watchpoints.
writer_outline: Lead with lower 2026 guidance alongside the Q3 beat.
Keep realized quarterly performance and future issuer expectations distinct.
Explain the revenue-cost tension without inventing complete causality.
Present operating-margin improvement as countercase and identify evidence needed to judge persistence.
rights: Facts-only original prose; no quotations or media reuse
